about:
# Ding!

A free, open-source leveling guide for **World of Warcraft: Forever** (client 1.60). Ding
shows what to do next, points the way with its own arrow and moves forward on its own as you
accept, complete and turn in quests. It is built from the ground up to be played **with a
gamepad**.

[Download on CurseForge](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/ding-xp-and-leveling-guide)

> **Version 1.8**, released during the Forever beta.
> **Alliance 1–60**: Human, Dwarf/Gnome and Night Elf starting zones up to level 20, then a
> common route to 60. **Horde 1–60**: Orc/Troll, Tauren and Undead starting zones up to
> level 20, then a common route to 60.
> Levels 30 to 60 have not been played in game yet (the beta stops at 30): they are checked
> by the offline tools only. Please report what you find in the
> [issues](https://github.com/moust4ki/DingGuideWoWForever/issues).

## Installation

Install Ding from [CurseForge](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/ding-xp-and-leveling-guide),
or copy the `Ding/` folder of this repository into `World of Warcraft/_forever_/Interface/AddOns/`
(during the beta: `_classic_beta_` instead of `_forever_`). That is all: Ding carries its own
game data, **QuestieDB is no longer needed** (you may remove it if no other addon uses it).

Ding has its own arrow: **TomTom is not needed**. If it is installed, its arrow can be used
instead from the *Arrow* tab of the settings (off by default).

## Features

- **Guides optimized for XP per hour.** The routes are generated offline from the game data:
  quests grouped to avoid back-and-forth, poor-value detours left out, never a quest above
  your level (one level above at most). The new quests of Forever are included.
- **Class quests.** A separate pack, *Ding! - Class quests* (*Guide* tab, under "Class"): the
  guide of your class and side, its important quest chains in level order. A druid's bear,
  aquatic and cat forms, a hunter's first pet, a warlock's demons and dreadsteed, a warrior's
  stances and Whirlwind weapon, a paladin's Redemption and charger, a shaman's totems, a
  rogue's poisons, the priests' and mages' race and class quests, with Forever's own (the
  Skyborne, the Forsaken paladins, the Alliance shamans...). Each chain says from which level
  it opens and what it teaches; you only see your class. Steps inside a dungeon show with the
  *Dungeon quests* option of the *Route* tab.
- **Dungeon quests.** A separate pack, *Ding! - Dungeon quests* (*Guide* tab, under
  "Dungeons"): one guide per dungeon for your side, listed by level. It takes you to every quest
  giver of the dungeon and through the chains that lead to them, then to the entrance, through
  the dungeon with a note for each quest (which boss drops what, where it waits), and back to the
  turn-ins. From Ragefire Chasm and the Deadmines to Scholomance and Stratholme, with Forever's
  own dungeons (the Hall of Thanes, the Ruins of Lordaeron, the Excavation Site, the City of
  Dalaran). Each chain says what it brings and when it is long or far; raids are not in it.
- **A setup assistant** at the first launch: four short screens, a few choices each, the
  recommended ones already selected. How you play (gamepad or keyboard and mouse), what Ding
  does for you (quests, gray items, repairs), your route (hearthstone, group quests, death
  skips), then the guide to start with. "Keep the recommended settings" ends it from any
  screen; everything else is on by default, and all of it can be changed later in the settings.
  Run it again from the *Guide* tab ("Run the setup assistant again") or with `/ding intro`.
- **Resumes where you really are.** Ding picks the guide for your race, class and level. When
  you resume, it first sends you to finish the guide's old quests still in your log, then
  skips what you have done.
- **Themes.** Pick the look in the settings (*Appearance*), with a live preview while you
  choose: **Forever · Halo** (the default: no frame, a soft veil under the text, the game's
  gold), **Forever · Slate** (a dark panel with gold hairlines), **Forever · Bands** (a band
  behind each line, outlined text for light scenes) or **Ding dark** (Ding!'s original
  look). The background's opacity follows the theme until you set your own. The arrow has its
  own picker (*Arrow and maps*): the theme's arrow, or any of the others (the gold arrow of
  Ding!'s icon among them), with any theme.
- **Guide window.** One line per action and objective, with counters (2/6), done / to do /
  not yet possible states and the guide's notes. Hover a line to see its quest (name, level,
  objectives); click it to send the arrow there. Right-click the window to mark the step as
  done or skip it for later: steps left by hand keep their own color (violet: marked done,
  amber: skipped); go back to such a step ("previous") to undo it, from the line under it or the
  same menu. Minimizes to a single line, automatically in combat if you want. Closing it
  hides the arrow too; the minimap button brings both back.
- **Waypoint arrow.** Distance and time to the target, in the theme's "turn around" color
  when it is behind you. Among the monsters you have to kill, it tells you you're in the area. When you
  die, it leads your ghost back to your corpse.
- **Automation.** Accepts and turns in the guide's quests when you talk to an NPC (you still
  choose your reward), catches up on missing prerequisite quests, can skip gray quests.
- **Quest item button.** A floating button with the item the step needs: one press of a
  gamepad button uses it. Shows the cooldown and when you are out of range.
- **NPC directory.** Bags full, out of food, a weapon to learn? The directory (its key
  binding, the pin button of the guide window, or `/ding find`) lists, anywhere in the world,
  the NPC of each kind that is the fewest seconds away: vendor, repair, food and drink,
  ammunition, reagents, poisons, innkeeper, flight master, class trainer, weapon masters by
  weapon, profession trainers by profession, trade supplies, bank, auction house, stable
  master. A second tab lists the capitals of your side and the neutral towns (Booty Bay,
  Gadgetzan, Ratchet, Everlook) with what each offers. Each row says how long it takes and by
  which way (flight, boat, zeppelin, tram, hearthstone). Pick one: the arrow takes you there
  leg by leg, the guide window says what to take, and the guide resumes once you talk to that
  NPC. When you carry (or a quest offers) a weapon your class can use but you have not
  learned, the guide window says so, why, and which weapon master teaches it; right-click it
  (Left in focus mode) never to see that weapon suggested again.
- **Report a problem.** An NPC missing, the arrow pointing to the wrong place, a quest not
  offered? The orange flag in the guide window's title bar ("Problem with this step?", beside the
  NPC directory's pin), its key binding or `/ding bug` writes a precise report for you: the step, where you stand, your
  quests and their counters, what the arrow points at, your route settings, never your
  character's name. See [Report a problem](#report-a-problem).
- **Minimap button.** Left-click for the settings, right-click to show or hide the guide.
- **Community guides.** Ding runs other guides too: install a guide pack and pick it in the
  settings (*Guide* tab, first list), then its section in the second list. See
  [Community guide packs](#community-guide-packs).
- **DingDB, an open game database.** Ding's game data (quests, NPCs, objects, items, places,
  names in 9 languages) is open: other addons can read it (`LibDingDB`), and anyone can correct
  it or add to it. See [docs/dingdb.md](https://github.com/moust4ki/DingGuideWoWForever/blob/main/docs/dingdb.md).
- **Languages.** English, French, German, Spanish (Spain and Latin America), Brazilian
  Portuguese, Korean, Simplified and Traditional Chinese: Ding follows your game's language.
  Quest, NPC and item names come from Ding's game data in that language. Each language has its own
  files; to add one, see [docs/SPEC.md](https://github.com/moust4ki/DingGuideWoWForever/blob/main/docs/SPEC.md#languages).

## With a gamepad

On first launch, **RB + Up** opens Ding's settings (LB + Up if you already use RB + Up); the
setup assistant shows it on its first screen (the D-pad picks a choice, A ticks it, LB / RB
change screens, Y keeps the recommended settings, B closes). In the **Keybinds** tab, bind "Next
step", "Previous step" and "Use the quest item" too: a single button, or two buttons (hold one,
press the other: LB + Up, LT + A…), which Ding watches itself and keeps from the game while you
hold the first; tap B to cancel, hold B to bind B itself. `/ding help` reminds you how to open
the settings.
Easy Controller and Ding work side by side: see
[docs/compatibility.md](https://github.com/moust4ki/DingGuideWoWForever/blob/main/docs/compatibility.md).
In the settings window: A selects, B closes, LB / RB change tabs, the D-pad picks and adjusts,
Y resets to default.

The guide window never takes a button away from the game. To browse it with the gamepad,
bind "Browse the guide with the gamepad" (focus mode): the D-pad picks a line, A sends the
arrow there (or uses the item), X shows its quest, LB / RB change steps, Y minimizes the
window, B gives the gamepad back to the game. Up from the first line, the focus reaches the
NPC directory's button, then the "Report a problem" flag beside it.

The NPC directory (bind "NPC directory", or use the guide window's pin button): LB / RB change
tabs, the D-pad picks, A opens a list or sends the arrow, B goes back or closes. To cancel a trip:
the "Cancel the trip" line under it in the guide window (a click, or A in focus mode), the first
entry of the right-click menu, the directory's first row, or `/ding cancel`; moving the guide
(next, skip, mark as done...) ends it too.

The settings also move the window, the arrow and the item button with the D-pad, set the
opacity and the size, minimize the guide in combat and pick the button names (Xbox or
PlayStation). They also open from the window's menu button, the minimap button or
*Options > AddOns > Ding*.

## With a keyboard and mouse

Everything works without a gamepad too. In the settings, click to choose, toggle or confirm
(click again when a button asks), right-click to put a setting back to its default or to
unbind a key, and press Escape to close. To bind a key, click its row and press the key. To
move the guide window, the arrow or the item button, drag it with the mouse, then click
Save. In the setup assistant, click a choice, Previous, Next or "Keep the recommended settings";
Escape closes it. Chosen "Keyboard and mouse" there, the Keybinds tab does not open after it.
The gamepad hints at the bottom ("A Open", "Y Reset"…) can be clicked too. Without a
gamepad plugged in, that help speaks of the mouse and the keyboard, and the buttons show no
gamepad button.

## Commands

`/ding` show/hide · `/ding config` settings · `/ding intro` (the setup assistant again) · `/ding list` (guides and their sections) ·
`/ding guide <id>` · `/ding where` (your position, for guide authors) · `/ding passages [n]` (the
lifts, gates and tunnels near you, for testers; the arrow points at the n-th) · `/ding import` (a guide as
text) · `/ding export [id]` (a guide as text) · `/ding find <text>` (the NPC directory: a service,
a weapon, a profession or a name, in your game's language or in English, such as
`/ding find gun`, `/ding find bank`, `/ding find Buliwyf`) · `/ding cancel` (end the directory's
trip: the arrow follows the guide again) · `/ding bug` (report a problem) · `/ding next` · `/ding prev` · `/ding skip` · `/ding back` · `/ding reset` (take the guide up
where you are) · `/ding scale <0.5-1.5>` · `/ding arrow` · `/ding arrowflip` ·
`/ding minimap` · `/ding debug`

## Report a problem

Something wrong with a step? Ding writes the report for you, in game:

1. Open **Report a problem with the guide**: the orange flag in the guide window's title bar
   ("Problem with this step?", beside the NPC directory's pin; with a gamepad, up from the first
   line in focus mode), its key binding
   (*Keybinds* tab: a button or two, like the others) or `/ding bug`.
2. The window shows what the report will contain: the guide, the step ("Step 19 / 161") and its
   place in the guide's file, where you stand, your character, the step's quests and their
   counters, what the arrow points at, the settings that change your route, Ding's and the
   game's versions. Never your character's name, your realm or your account.
3. Pick what went wrong ("The NPC is not there", "The arrow points to the wrong place", "The
   quest is not offered", "Something else") and, if you can type, add a few words.
4. **Create the text**: the window shows, in order, the address of a
   [new report on GitHub](https://github.com/moust4ki/DingGuideWoWForever/issues/new?template=ding-report.yml)
   to open, then the text to paste into it. Each has a button that selects it; copy with
   Ctrl+C (an addon cannot copy for you). The text's first line can be the title.

No keyboard at hand? Ding keeps your last 20 reports in
`WTF\Account\<account>\SavedVariables\Ding.lua` (written when you log out or reload): send that
file instead.

## Community guide packs

Anyone can write a guide for Ding and share it as a **guide pack**: a small addon of Lua
files with quest ids, places and notes, which Ding plays like its own guide. Once
installed, a pack shows up in the settings (*Guide* tab) next to Ding's guide.

**Write a pack:** [docs/guide-packs.md](https://github.com/moust4ki/DingGuideWoWForever/blob/main/docs/guide-packs.md) explains every file, step by
step, how to test it in the game and how to check it offline. A working example to start
from: [examples/DingExamplePack](https://github.com/moust4ki/DingGuideWoWForever/blob/main/examples/DingExamplePack).

**Or a guide as text, with an AI:** [docs/create-a-guide-with-ai.md](https://github.com/moust4ki/DingGuideWoWForever/blob/main/docs/create-a-guide-with-ai.md)
gives the format, a complete example and a prompt ready to copy. Paste the result in the
game with `/ding import`: Ding checks every id and lists what is wrong, step by step.

**Known packs:** none yet. Published one? Open an
[issue](https://github.com/moust4ki/DingGuideWoWForever/issues) titled `Guide pack: <name>` and it
will be listed here.

## Development

Nothing runs in the game here: the offline tools load Ding with a mocked WoW API and play
every guide. See [tools/README.md](https://github.com/moust4ki/DingGuideWoWForever/blob/main/tools/README.md) and [CLAUDE.md](https://github.com/moust4ki/DingGuideWoWForever/blob/main/CLAUDE.md).
Every pull request runs the whole suite (`.github/workflows/tests.yml`); pushing a `v*` tag
publishes the release on CurseForge and GitHub once the suite passes
(`.github/workflows/release.yml`).

## License

Ding is free software, released under the **GNU GPL v3** (see [LICENSE](https://github.com/moust4ki/DingGuideWoWForever/blob/main/LICENSE)): you may
use, modify and redistribute it, provided you publish your modified versions under the same
license, with their source code.

Everything built on Ding stays free: a guide pack for Ding (an addon that calls
`Ding.RegisterGuidePack` and `Ding.RegisterGuide`) is a derivative work and must be released
under the GPL v3 as well. There is no exception.

The Noto Sans fonts in `Ding/Media/Fonts` are under the SIL Open Font License 1.1
(`OFL.txt`). TomTom is a separate addon; Ding ships none of its code.

### Credits

DingDB, Ding's game data (`Ding/DB`: quests, NPCs, objects, items, places and their names), is built
from the database of [Questie](https://github.com/Questie/Questie) and
[QuestieDB](https://github.com/Questie/QuestieDB), released under the GNU GPL v3: thanks to
their authors and contributors. See [`Ding/DB/CREDITS.md`](https://github.com/moust4ki/DingGuideWoWForever/blob/main/Ding/DB/CREDITS.md).

# Changelog

## v1.8.1

Nothing else to install: QuestieDB is no longer needed, and TomTom stays optional.

- Faster again: since v1.7.1, checking whether a quest objective is done rebuilt the list of
  every place its monsters stand each time (on level steps, for each quest of your log). Ding
  reads the objective's text first and keeps that list once built.

## v1.8.0

Nothing else to install: QuestieDB is no longer needed, and TomTom stays optional.

- **Problem with this step?** An orange flag in the guide window's title bar, right beside the
  NPC directory's pin (with a gamepad: up from the first line in focus mode), its own key binding
  (Settings > Keybinds, a button or two like the others) and `/ding bug`. A window shows in plain
  words what the report will contain: the guide, the step and its place in the guide's file,
  where you stand, your character's level, race, class and side, the step's quests and the ones
  of your log the next steps need, with their counters, what the arrow points at, the settings
  that change your route, Ding's and the game's versions. Never your character's name, your
  realm or your account.
- Pick what went wrong among four ready answers (handy with a gamepad) and add your own words if
  you can type, then **Create the text**: 1. the address of the GitHub page to open, 2. the text
  to paste into it, each selected by its button for Ctrl+C (an addon cannot copy for you). Ding
  keeps your last 20 reports in its saved variables (`WTF\Account\<account>\SavedVariables\Ding.lua`),
  so a player without a keyboard can send that file instead; "Restore all defaults" keeps them.

## v1.7.1

Nothing else to install: QuestieDB is no longer needed, and TomTom stays optional.

- The arrow no longer leads to monsters you have already killed enough of, when the game names
  them in your language and Ding only knows their English name (Forever's own monsters, the
  Skyborne start among them): it matches the quest's objectives by their order too. Their
  marks and counters above the nameplates come back the same way.
- "Choose quest rewards" never takes a piece your class cannot wear (a druid's reward was taken
  in mail): only what you can wear counts as an upgrade, and when none is, the reward that
  sells for the most among what you can use. The chat says which reward Ding took and why.

## v1.7.0

Nothing else to install: QuestieDB is no longer needed, and TomTom stays optional.

- **Dungeon quests**: a new pack, **Ding! - Dungeon quests** (Settings > Guide, under
  "Dungeons"), with one guide per dungeon for your side, listed by level (the ones above your
  level are greyed, you can still pick them). Each guide takes you to every quest giver of that
  dungeon and through the chains that lead to them, in an order that keeps the trips short, then
  to the dungeon's entrance, then through the dungeon with a note for each quest (which boss or
  monster drops what, where it waits), and back to the turn-ins and the quests they open. Every
  dungeon from Ragefire Chasm, the Deadmines and Wailing Caverns to Blackrock Depths, Lower
  Blackrock Spire, Dire Maul, Scholomance and Stratholme, and Forever's own: the Hall of Thanes,
  the Ruins of Lordaeron, the Excavation Site of the Wetlands and the City of Dalaran.
- The first step of each chain says what it brings (a weapon of your choice, armor of your
  kind, a ring, a big amount of XP) and when it is long or far away; very long or far chains are
  optional and say why. A quest that starts from a drop shows only once the drop is in your bags.
  Raids, the Upper Spire and the level 60 armor-set chains are not in the pack.
- A step that takes you to a dungeon's entrance now passes once you are inside: the game gives
  no position in a dungeon, and the step stayed on screen for the whole run.
- "Take this guide up where I am" keeps your place: it stops only on a quest of your log still
  to finish or a quest of the route you never took. With "Elite quests" turned on, it used to
  send you back to the first elite quest of the section.
- The guide window stays as it is in combat: minimizing it there is now an option, off by
  default (Settings > Appearance, "Minimize the guide in combat"). It was on for everyone: turn it
  on again there if you liked it.
- The arrow says "You're here" 6 yards from the place or the NPC (it was 10, and the arrow faded
  while you still had a few steps to walk), and "You're in the area" 25 yards from the monsters
  or the objects to gather (it was 40, more than an attack's reach).
- The aids are on for a new install: the quest marks and counters above the monsters, the line
  in their tooltip, and enemy nameplates shown farther. The game hides the enemy nameplates
  until you press V: Ding shows them once so that its counters appear, and says so in the chat.
- Upstairs and downstairs: when the NPC or the object waits on another floor, the arrow no
  longer says "You're here" in the middle of the building. It says "The NPC is one floor up",
  "at the top" or "one floor down", and stays on screen until you find the stairs.

## v1.6.1

Nothing else to install: QuestieDB is no longer needed, and TomTom stays optional.

- Gamepad: while you hold the first button of one of Ding's combinations (RB of RB + Up), the
  game's own combinations work again: LB + RB + Left / Right (the action bar's pages), LB + RB +
  Down (the chat)... Ding kept every button while it waited for the second one. With a Ding
  window open, the buttons the window does not use go on to the game too.

## v1.6.0

Nothing else to install: QuestieDB is no longer needed, and TomTom stays optional.

- **Class quests**: a new pack, **Ding! - Class quests** (Settings > Guide, under "Class"),
  with one guide for your class and side: its important quest chains in level order, from the
  level they open. Druid: bear form, cure poison, aquatic form, Forever's Great Cat Spirit,
  Torwa Pathfinder. Hunter: your first pet. Mage: the robes, Tabetha's wand, the Magecraft
  chain. Paladin: Redemption, Verigan's Fist, the warhorse, the Mightstone, the charger.
  Priest: your first robe and your race's prayers. Rogue: Pick Lock, your poisons, the Azure
  Key. Shaman: the earth, fire, water and air totems. Warlock: the voidwalker, the succubus,
  the felhunter, the felsteed, Niby's quests, the dreadsteed. Warrior: Defensive and Berserker
  Stances, the Whirlwind weapon. Forever's own class quests are in: the Skyborne's, the
  Forsaken paladins' story, the Alliance shamans' totems, the Human and Gnome hunters' pets,
  the Syndicate of Ravenholdt for rogues...
- Each chain says, under its first step, from which level it opens and what it is for ("From
  level 10: the chain that teaches Bear Form"), and the step that teaches it says so. You only
  see your own class's guide; pick your leveling guide again in Settings > Guide when you are
  done. Quests inside a dungeon show when that dungeon is on in Settings > Route.
- **Wetlands (27-29)**: Carnage, the last quest Rethiel the Greenwarden gives, now comes after
  Blisters on the Land is turned in (he does not offer it before), and as an elite quest: it
  shows only when **Elite quests** is on in Settings > Route.
- A step you marked done by hand keeps its mark when a new version of Ding writes the guide again
  and the step moves: the mark used to stay on the step number, and fell on another step
  ("marked as done by hand" on a step you never touched).
- A turn-in step passed because you already turned the quest in now says "already done"
  instead of "it does not concern you now".
- The ring around the arrow's target on the minimap sits on the target in a city's inside view
  too (Ironforge): it used the outdoor scale there and only reached the target once you were
  on it.

## v1.5.0

Nothing else to install: QuestieDB is no longer needed, and TomTom stays optional.

## v1.5.0

Nothing else to install: QuestieDB is no longer needed, and TomTom stays optional.

- **Themes**: choose the look of Ding! in Settings > Appearance. While you go from one theme to
  the next, the guide window, the arrow and the settings show it at once; A (or a click) keeps
  it, leaving the themes without it brings yours back.
  - **Forever · Halo**: no frame, a soft dark veil under the text, the game's gold and its own
    font for titles, light gamepad buttons like the game's.
  - **Forever · Slate**: a dark panel with thin gold lines, lines tinted by their state, a gold
    marker on the gamepad's focus, the arrow's text on a small plate.
  - **Forever · Bands**: no window, a band behind each line, outlined text that stays readable
    on snow and sand, a blue accent.
  - **Ding dark**: the look of the previous versions.
- **The default look is now Forever · Halo, for everyone**, also if you played an earlier
  version: to get the old look back, pick **Ding dark** in Settings > Appearance. The
  background's opacity follows each theme (Halo: 60 %) until you move the slider yourself; if
  you had chosen your own, it is kept.
- Quest names are in the game's quest gold, items and monsters in light blue; in the Forever
  themes nothing still to do is red anymore (red reads as danger in the game).
- The card shown when you hover a line of the guide window (X in focus mode) now has the
  theme's look.
- **The arrow's look** has its own picker in Settings > Arrow and maps: the theme's arrow (the
  default), Halo's gold arrow, Slate's, Bands', Ding!'s, the new **Gold** arrow or the game's
  minimap arrow, with any theme; the real arrow shows each one while you choose. If you had
  picked the minimap arrow, you keep it.
- **A new icon**: Ding!'s arrow in gold, with a burst of light, on the minimap button and in the
  AddOns list.
- The arrow says where under the target's name: the flight master and its zone, the zone of a
  target outside yours, or the stop of the farming loop ("Farming loop: stop 2 of 10").
- **Keybinds with the gamepad fixed**: a button you bind now replaces the old one (it used to
  be added beside it, and the row kept showing the first one, often "RB"). **Any two gamepad
  buttons make a shortcut**: hold one, press the other (LB + Up, RB + Up, LT + A, LT + D-pad
  down…); Ding! watches them itself, like Easy Controller's RB + Down, and while you hold the
  first button it keeps the second one from the game (out of combat). A button the game's
  gamepad interface or another addon (Easy Controller...) also uses is named, and A binds it
  anyway. Tap B to cancel, hold B to bind B itself. If an action of Ding! ended up on several buttons, its row says "and 2
  more": bind it again, or press Y, to clean it up.
- **RB + Up opens Ding!**: "Open Ding! settings" gets **RB + Up** on the gamepad (LB + Up if you
  already use RB + Up), and the setup assistant shows it on its first screen; with the keyboard
  and mouse, it names the minimap button and the guide window's menu button. `/ding help` says
  it too. A button you gave it yourself is kept.
- **Ding!'s windows keep their buttons**: in focus mode, the settings, the directory and the
  setup assistant, the D-pad, A, B and the shoulders are Ding!'s while the window is open, even
  with the game's gamepad interface and Easy Controller (the D-pad used to cast the gamepad
  bar's spells in focus mode).
- **Easy Controller and Ding! side by side**: Ding! never changes the game's gamepad settings
  and its default button never takes a key Easy Controller uses; Ding!'s windows work as usual
  with Easy Controller on.
- Settings: on a line with a description, the two lines are centered on the line and its check
  box (the label used to touch the line's frame).
